source.section: Form MO-1040 PDF p2 Lines 1-8 and 14-15, PDF p3 Lines 25-30 (instructions PDF pp6-9); Instructions PDF p8 Line 14 standard deductions; PDF p21 Tax Rate Chart Sections A and B; record base.deductions; Form MO-A PDF p3 Part 3 Section C; instructions PDF p17 Section C Lines 1-2 and Worksheet for Lines 1 and 2; Reference Guide PDF p9; record social_security_retirement_subtraction; Form MO-A PDF p3 Part 3 Section A Lines 1-5; instructions PDF p17; Reference Guide PDF p9 (47,633 per taxpayer); record public_pension_subtraction

worked: Single, age 67. Same person, pension over 47,633: Line 3 reduces the exemption, not the pension, so the two together are 47,633. Federal taxable Social Security: other income 70,000.00 + half of benefits 15,000.00 = provisional 85,000.00; 85% x (85,000.00 - 34,000.00) + 4,500.00 = 47,850.00, limited to 85% x 30,000.00 = 25,500.00. Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = pensions 60,000.00 + taxable Social Security 25,500.00 + interest 10,000.00 = 95,500.00. Federal taxable income = 95,500.00 - standard deduction 17,750.00 (including the additional amount for age 65) = 77,750.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Form MO-1040 Line 1 federal AGI 95,500.00. Line 2 additions 0.00. Line 3 total income 95,500.00. Line 4 subtractions 0.00. Line 6 Missouri adjusted gross income 95,500.00 - 0.00 = 95,500.00. MO-A Part 3 Section C (Y, age 67): Line 1 25,500.00; Line 3 25,500.00 (62 or older by December 31). Section C Line 4 total 25,500.00. Section A (Y): Line 1 60,000.00; Line 2 lesser of that or 47,633.00 = 47,633.00; Line 3 25,500.00; Line 4 22,133.00. Section A Line 5 total 22,133.00. Projection, best_of_group evaluated for each person separately: the filer: larger of Social Security exemption 25,500.00 and public pension 47,633.00 = 47,633.00; total 47,633.00, the same as Section A Line 5 + Section C Line 4. Form MO-1040 Line 8 pension and Social Security exemption 47,633.00. Lines 9-13 federal income tax deduction not applied (not modelled; the household's federal tax is not an input). Line 14 standard deduction 15,750.00 + 1 x 2,000.00 for age 65 or older = 17,750.00. Line 26 subtotal 95,500.00 - 47,633.00 - 17,750.00 = 30,117.00. Line 29 taxable income 30,117.00. Tax by the bands (0% to 1,313): 2% x 1,313.00 = 26.26 + 2.5% x 1,313.00 = 32.825 + 3% x 1,313.00 = 39.39 + 3.5% x 1,313.00 = 45.955 + 4% x 1,313.00 = 52.52 + 4.5% x 1,313.00 = 59.085 + 4.7% x 20,926.00 = 983.522; total 1239.557 = 1,239.56. The chart and Tax Calculation Worksheet (instructions p21) round to the dollar and give 1240; expected keeps the bands. state_agi (after every relief, as the check format defines it) = Line 6 95,500.00 - Line 8 47,633.00 = 47,867.00; the form's Missouri AGI is Line 6, 95,500.00.
accepted_approximations: The chart's cumulative amounts are rounded to whole dollars and the tax to the nearest dollar; the bands here do neither.
The federal income tax deduction is not applied (not_modelled).

The public pension exemption and the Social Security exemption share a best_of_group, each person separately. Form MO-A takes the lesser of the pension or 47,633 and subtracts that person's Social Security exemption (Section A Lines 2-4), which reduces the exemption, not the cap, so cap_reduced_by would be wrong. The two exemptions together come to the larger of the Social Security exemption and the lesser of the pension or 47,633, which is what the group gives when evaluated per person.
